active.description:
If true, apply this rule to conversations. Otherwise, this rule is
inactive.
active.rationale: This attribute controls the operational state of the rule and has no direct security impact.

assessment_rule_id.description:
A unique ID for the new AssessmentRule. This ID will become the final
component of the AssessmentRule's resource name. If no ID is specified,
a server-generated ID will be used.

This value should be 4-64 characters and must match the regular
expression '^[A-Za-z0-9]{4,64}$'.
assessment_rule_id.rationale: Used for identification purposes only. No direct security impact.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

display_name.description: Display Name of the assessment rule.
display_name.rationale: Used for identification purposes only. No direct security impact.

location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Used for identification purposes only. No direct security impact.

sample_rule.conversation_filter.description:
To specify the filter for the conversions that should apply this sample
rule. An empty filter means this sample rule applies to all conversations.
sample_rule.conversation_filter.rationale: A free-form expression selecting which conversations the sample rule applies to. This is a team data-scoping choice, not a structural security control, and a generic platform policy cannot meaningfully constrain an arbitrary filter string.

sample_rule.dimension.description:
Group by dimension to sample the conversation. If no dimension is
provided, the sampling will be applied to the project level.
Current supported dimensions is 'quality_metadata.agent_info.agent_id'.
sample_rule.dimension.rationale: Defines conversation sampling grouping only. No direct security impact.

sample_rule.sample_percentage.description:
Percentage of conversations that we should sample  based on the dimension
between [0, 100].
sample_rule.sample_percentage.rationale: Sets what fraction of conversations the assessment rule samples. This is a team data-management/operational tuning choice with no secure direction to enforce, so it matches no policy archetype.

sample_rule.sample_row.description: Number of the conversations that we should sample based on the dimension.
sample_rule.sample_row.rationale: Defines sample data representation only. No direct security impact.

schedule_info.end_time.description:
End time of the schedule. If not specified, will keep scheduling new
pipelines for execution until the schedule is no longer active or deleted.
A timestamp in RFC3339 UTC "Zulu" format, with nanosecond resolution and
up to nine fractional digits. Examples: "2014-10-02T15:01:23Z" and "2014-10-02T15:01:23.045123456Z".
schedule_info.end_time.rationale: Defines schedule end time only. No direct security impact.

schedule_info.schedule.description:
The groc expression.
Format: 'every number [synchronized]'
Cron syntax is not supported.
Time units can be: minutes, hours
Synchronized is optional and indicates that the schedule should be
synchronized to the start of the interval: every 5 minutes synchronized
means 00:00, 00:05 ...
Otherwise the start time is random within the interval.
Example: 'every 5 minutes'
could be  00:02, 00:07, 00:12, ...
schedule_info.schedule.rationale: Defines the scheduling logic for the assessment rule. No direct security impact.

schedule_info.start_time.description:
Start time of the schedule. If not specified, will start as soon as the
schedule is created.
A timestamp in RFC3339 UTC "Zulu" format, with nanosecond resolution and
up to nine fractional digits. Examples: "2014-10-02T15:01:23Z" and "2014-10-02T15:01:23.045123456Z".
schedule_info.start_time.rationale: Defines schedule start time only. No direct security impact.

schedule_info.time_zone.description:
The timezone to use for the groc expression.
If not specified, defaults to UTC.
schedule_info.time_zone.rationale: Defines the timezone for the scheduling logic. No direct security impact.
